diagnostics.message: :resource.null_resource.wait_for_cluster: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_eks_cluster.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

The explicit `depends_on = [aws_eks_cluster.this[0], ...]` on null_resource.wait_for_cluster duplicates an implicit dependency: its `provisioner "local-exec"` already sets `ENDPOINT = aws_eks_cluster.this[0].endpoint`, so Terraform orders null_resource.wait_for_cluster after aws_eks_cluster.this anyway. Only the `aws_security_group_rule.cluster_private_access` entry carries information.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers can launch instances before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy is attached: the launch configuration only reaches aws_iam_role.workers through the instance profile, which is a sibling of the policy attachment, so no ordering exists. Worker instances run bootstrap.sh, which calls `eks:DescribeCluster` (granted by AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy); without it bootstrap fails and the nodes never join the cluster. The node_groups submodule explicitly guards this same race via `ng_depends_on`, but the self-managed ASGs do not.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers_launch_template can launch instances before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy is attached — the launch template only reaches aws_iam_role.workers via aws_iam_instance_profile.workers_launch_template, which is a sibling of the policy attachment. Worker bootstrap requires `eks:DescribeCluster` from that policy; without it the instance bootstrap fails and nodes never join. The node_groups submodule guards this race with `ng_depends_on`; these self-managed ASGs are unguarded.
